reasons: The rule expects a post-termination transition/data-return obligation in a hosted-services MSA; none of the cited paragraphs create one — Section 10.1 only presupposes 'any agreed transition period', Section 10.2 addresses Deliverables and refunds, and Section 16.5 expressly excludes Customer Data from its return-or-destroy duty by deferring to Sections 11 and 15, so the 'missing' classification is supported and neither preferred nor fallback is met.

The inserted Section 10.3 tracks the model language closely (6 months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, subsequent deletion with written certification) and is placed in the correct termination section as an addition only, leaving existing text untouched — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Minor drafting variations (return 'within thirty (30) days of Customer's request' and a backups/legal-retention carve-out mirroring Section 16.5) are reasonable and consistent with the contract's own conventions; they do not undercut the preferred position or drift into walk-away territory.
The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the correct prefix, explains the gap, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day fallback.
